questions.q: Two vectors <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>X</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">Y</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover></math> have equal magnitude. The magnitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">X</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo mathvariant="italic">-</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">Y</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> times the magnitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">X</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi>Y</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></math>. The angle between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>X</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">Y</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover></math> is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given X=Y

X2+Y2-2×Ycosθ

=nX2+Y2+2×Ycosθ

Square both sides

2X2(1-cosθ)=n2·2X2(1+cosθ)

1-cosθ=n2+n2cosθ

cosθ=1-n21+n2

θ=cos-1n2-1-n2-1

questions.q: Two vectors <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> have equal magnitudes. The magnitude of <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math> is ' <math><mi>n</mi></math> ' times the magnitude of <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math> . The angle between <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: A→+B→=nA→-B→, so, the magnitudes of this will be given as,

A2+B2+2ABcosθ=nA2+B2-2ABcosθ;where θ is the angle between A→ and B→.

Also, A→=B→,

2A2+2A2cosθ=n2A2-2A2cosθ

Squaring both sides:

2A21+cosθ=n22A21-cosθ

cosθ=n2-1n2+1

i.e., θ=cos-1n2-1n2+1

Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For two vectors to be perpendicular, their dot product is equal to zero.

So, P→·Q→=0

⇒i^+2mj^+mk^·4i^-2j^+mk^=0⇒4-4m+m2=0⇒m-22=0⇒m=2

questions.q: The energy of a system is given as $\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{t})=\alpha^3 \mathrm{e}^{-\beta t}$, where t is the time and $\beta=0.3 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The errors in the measurement of $\alpha$ and $t$ are $1.2 \%$ and $1.6 \%$, respectively. At $t=5 \mathrm{~s}$, maximum percentage error in the energy is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& d E=3 \alpha^2 d \alpha e^{-\beta t}+\alpha^3 e^{-\beta t}(-\beta) d t \\
& \frac{d E}{E}=\frac{3 d \alpha}{\alpha}+(-\beta) d t \\
& \frac{\Delta E}{E}=\frac{3 \Delta \alpha}{\alpha}+\beta \Delta t
\end{aligned}$
(\%) $\Delta t=1.6 \% \times 5=8 \%\%\left(\frac{3 \Delta \alpha}{\alpha}\right)=3 \times 1.2 \%=3.6 \%$
Putting values we get
$\Rightarrow 3.6+8 \times 0.3=6 \%$

questions.solution:
In addition or subtractions, final answer must contain the equal numbers of digits after decimal as the adding or subtracting quantities among which is having the lowest numbers of digits after decimal.

The Least number of  significant digit after decimal  in the above expression is 1 So, Sum should conatian 1 significant digit after decimal.

The Least number of  significant digit after decimal  in the above expression is 0 So, Sum should conatian 0 significant digit after decimal

Now particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is moving normal to the plane which contains vector <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>.</mo></math> Similarly particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is moving normal to the plane which contains vector <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>C</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>.</mo></math> The angle between the direction of motion of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mfenced><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><menclose notation="bottom"><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mo> </mo></menclose></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>.</mo></math>

questions.solution:
Unit vector in the direction of P→×Q→ is n^=P→×Q→|P→×Q→|.

Here, P→×Q→=i^j^k^332432.5=3i^2+j^2-3k^

And P→×Q→=322+122+32=4=2

⇒P→×Q→|P→×Q→|=123i^2+j^2-3k^

=14(3i^+j^-23k^)  ⇒x=4

If percentage error in measurement of  '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>' and '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>' are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>%</mo></math>, respectively, then the percentage error for '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math>' will be _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: z=a2x3y12

Relative error is given by 

∆zz=3×∆xx+12×∆yy

Now, maximum percentage error in z is 

∆zz×100=34+122×100

=18%.
